text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: realtime-p95-detector fired for route /v1/generate (prod-us-east-1). p95 jumped above configured alert threshold (800ms) for the last 3 min window. p99 also rising. Auto-checks attached.
Oncall - Nate H: on it. paging SRE Lead and Maria. tagging support. :eyes:
Maria S: seeing it on the graph too — p95 ~920ms (was ~210ms baseline), p99 ~4.8s. streaming connections show increased stalls. link: https://dash.redwood-infra/p95/route/generate?range=15m
Kevin L: I already got a page. quick checks: GPU util, request queue depth, redis latencies. running `kubectl top pods -n redwood-infer | grep runtime` and `curl -s http://router/metrics | jq '.request_queue'`
Oncall - Nate H: thanks. Kevin can you paste the results when you have them. Maria can you check recent deploys and config rollouts? Priya, can support start triage with customer-impact assessment (who's affected)?
Kevin L: gpu utils look normal for the cluster (60-70% for runtime pool), but runtimes show increased blocked threads. request queue depth spiked to ~420 (baseline 40). redis p95 for kvcache up to 300ms. snippet:
```
# runtimes queue snapshot
runtime-01 queue: 120
runtime-02 queue: 98
runtime-03 queue: 200
redis-kv p95: 305ms
```
Maria S: no deploys in the last 2 hours. routing config unchanged. I see elevated prefix cache misses for some keys. cache hit-rate dropped from 91% -> 62% over the spike window.
Oncall - Nate H: ok that points to cache pressure/backpressure causing extra compute and queueing. Priya — what customers are hitting the route the most right now?
Support Bot: Top customers by request volume in last 10m: "acme-analytics" (18%), "widget-co" (12%), "dev-sandbox" (8%). No current P1s raised by customers yet. Incidents alerts auto-forwarded to their on-call.
Priya R: pinged acme-analytics and widget-co. acme-analytics reports some 5xx streaming disconnects and slow completions in last 10m. I'll open support tickets and set their severity to 'investigating'.
SRE Lead: suggested mitigation path: 1) increase route fallback to smaller/quantized model variant (temporary) 2) flush redis prefix cache or scale redis 3) reduce batching window on router to avoid head-of-line stalls. Which is fastest to apply?
Kevin L: fastest is to reduce batching window from 100ms -> 20ms for affected route (config push). second fastest is route fallback (we can flip traffic to model-x-quant-8 in the routing table). flushing redis is disruptive but possible.
Oncall - Nate H: let's do reduced batching first, then route fallback if no improvement in 3-5 min. Maria — can you flip batching? Kevin — prepare the route fallback but don't switch yet.
Maria S: applying batching change now.
Incident Bot: Deploy bot: config update started for route /v1/generate (batch_window_ms: 100 -> 20).
Maria S: change rolled to 50% of routers (canary) in us-east-1. monitoring.
Kevin L: prepping route fallback command, ready to execute. adding runbook note: `routerctl set-route /v1/generate model=model-x-quant-8 --weight 100 --reason "mitigation: p95 spike"`
Maria S: on-canary graphs: p95 dropped to ~480ms on canary path after batching change. p99 down to ~2.2s. global p95 now ~720ms (from 920ms). improvement visible.
Oncall - Nate H: good signal. keep monitoring for 2 more minutes. Priya — confirm customers see improvement?
Priya R: acme-analytics says latencies improving for some requests, but some streaming clients still see stalls. they sent logs showing partial frames then disconnects.
SRE Lead: streaming stalls could be due to KV cache misses causing long-model-inits for some request prefixes. If batching reduction doesn't fully mitigate, flip fallback for high-volume customers or enable per-tenant routing to smaller model.
Kevin L: ready to flip fallback for traffic from acme-analytics only: `routerctl set-route /v1/generate --selector tenant=acme-analytics model=model-x-quant-8 --weight 100`
Oncall - Nate H: hold. let's wait 3 more minutes. if p95 < 600ms and p99 < 2s we'll keep reduced batching as full rollout; else do targeted fallback.
Incident Bot: automated check @ +3m: p95=610ms, p99=1.9s, request queue depth down to 120, redis p95 120ms.
Maria S: given that, I'm going to roll batching change to 100% in us-east-1.
Maria S: rolled to 100%. monitoring. p95 steady at ~580ms, p99 ~1.7s. good.
Oncall - Nate H: no further mitigations yet. escalate to SRE Lead for post-incident review and root cause once things are stable. start timeline capture.
SRE Lead: I'll take handoff. Nate — summarize timeline and actions in the incident doc. assign postmortem owner (Maria) and include eval tests for cache hit regression. tagging infra and runtime teams.
Oncall - Nate H: summary: detection -> batching canary -> global rollout -> queue + redis improvement -> customer impacts reduced. mitigation avoided model fallback. Estimated impact: ~12% of requests experienced >1s latency during spike window. no broad customer outages, multiple customers saw streaming glitches. next: postmortem, slow-eval on prefix cache, consider autoscaling redis and add caching alerts.
Support Bot: auto-created incident ticket #INC-2026-1796011000, severity: P2, assigned: Maria S, sla: 72h.
Priya R: I'll continue customer comms and patch notes. acme-analytics asked for a warm-cache run later; scheduling.
SRE Lead: thanks team. Nate — hand off to me for the full RCA. if anything regresses ping on this thread. otherwise we mark resolved and start postmortem.
Oncall - Nate H: handing over to SRE Lead. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
Incident Bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. will auto-close if metrics stable for 2 hours.
